name: Status quo: only TERRESTRIAL_HEX is a political land target
historical_correctness: POOR at small scale. Loses 1.0-2.0 per cent of authorised land on large islands but 14.8 per cent of Malta and 29.7 per cent of Gozo. The error is scale-dependent, which is the worst property for a model that will meet more small islands.
gameplay_semantics: Clean and already documented; every land target is a majority-land hex.
verdict: Keep as the default only if the scale-dependence is accepted and documented in the scenario contract.

name: Any hex with land_area > 0 becomes a political land target; physical water class unchanged
historical_correctness: BEST: recovers all 5,644 km2. Every square kilometre of authorised land becomes ownable.
gameplay_semantics: Breaks the documented invariant 'an OCEAN hex is never itself a land-control target'. A hex that is 99 per cent sea would carry a land controller.
movement_implications: None today, but it pre-commits the future movement model to answering what a 1-per-cent-land owned hex means.
data_size: +3,014 control rows (+6 per cent) for the seven landmasses produced so far.
migration_cost: Moderate: scenario_pipeline.py:934 must stop using is_terrestrial_hex as the political gate, and every earlier stage's regression counts change.
compatibility: Breaks the MAPGEN-006R invariant; needs an explicit amendment, not a quiet edit.
island_overlays: Would collide with overlay units on the same ocean hexes unless deduplicated.
mixed_controller_risk: HIGH: 456 of the withheld hexes carry land of more than one component.
verdict: Historically ideal, architecturally the most expensive. Not recommended without a deliberate revision of the target contract.

name: A new LAND_BEARING_HEX / COASTAL_LAND_FRAGMENT target type, distinct from TERRESTRIAL_HEX
historical_correctness: EQUAL to B: the same 5,644 km2 becomes addressable, but as a distinct kind of target that is honest about being a fragment.
gameplay_semantics: Preserves the invariant: the OCEAN hex is still not a land-control target; a NAMED FRAGMENT on it is. Same move the project already made for sub-hex islands.
movement_implications: None today; leaves the future movement model free to treat fragments differently from full land hexes.
data_size: +3,014 rows of a new target type; existing TERRESTRIAL_HEX counts unchanged, so every earlier regression number survives.
migration_cost: Moderate: one new value in TARGET_TYPES, one new id space, validator extension.
compatibility: Additive. No existing row changes meaning.
island_overlays: Composable: a fragment is keyed by (hex, component) so it cannot collide with an overlay unit for a different component.
mixed_controller_risk: MANAGEABLE: keying by component makes two controllers on one hex explicit rather than a conflict.
verdict: RECOMMENDED. It is the same architectural move the project already made once, it keeps every existing count intact, and it makes the fragment visible rather than silently owned.

name: Reuse the existing ISLAND_COMPONENT / overlay target
gameplay_semantics: Would require a component to be both represented_by_terrestrial_hex and separately targetable.
migration_cost: Looks cheapest but is not: it requires weakening no_duplicate_overlay_for_large_islands, the very rule that stops a landmass being counted twice.
compatibility: Directly contradicts an existing validation check.
island_overlays: Would double-represent Great Britain, Iceland and every other produced landmass.
mixed_controller_risk: HIGH - the component granularity is wrong; one component would own fragments in hundreds of hexes with no per-hex identity.
verdict: REJECTED on the evidence of the project's own anti-double-count rule.
